title: Survivors: attributes, skills, traits (basic)
summary: The Survivor record every other system reads: name, health, mood, a handful of 0–20 skills and 1–3 traits that bend the numbers. Rolled from the run's seed so a seed always gives the same crew.
whyHere: First gameplay card: needs, health, work, inventory and combat units all hang off a Survivor. It only needs IDs, content and RNG from L1, so it can start as soon as those exist.
sliceScope: 4 survivors rolled at new game. 6 skills (Shooting, Melee, Medicine, Building, Farming, Scavenging), each 0–20: a roll of 0–9 plus 1–2 specialties +3..7. 6 traits from JSON (Tough, Frail, Quick Healer, Glutton, Brave, Coward), 1–2 each. Health 0–100, mood 0–100. No XP yet: skills are fixed for the slice. No STR/DEX-style attributes: the prototype gets by on skills + traits, so do the same.
fullScope: 12 skills 0–20 that grow by use (XP to level up = 40 + 0.32×L³, 11 XP for a full day's job, daily caps 20/30/25), teaching, books and perks (surv.skills); ~30 traits with tiers I–III and point costs; backgrounds, appearance and custom crews (meta.modes). Families, recruits and relations come in surv.family/surv.relations.

data: content/skills.json: id, display name, art key (6 entries for the slice)
content/traits.json: id, name, description, opposites (Tough vs Frail), and a list of effects {stat, op: mul|add, value}
Survivor runtime class in BrokenState.Sim (Id, Name, Skills dict, Traits list, Health, Mood, Location) + save mapping
content/names.json: first/last name pools for the generator
backend: SurvivorFactory.Create(Rng, quality): skills, specialties, traits (no opposite pairs), name; uses its own RNG stream
TraitFx.Mul(survivor, stat) / Add(...): the ONE place trait effects are read (e.g. "woundMult" Tough ×0.75, Frail ×1.25)
Skills.Effective(s, skill): base level + trait add, clamped 0–20; SkillMult(level) for work/aim formulas
Roster queries: Alive(), AtBase(baseId), InParty(partyId); SurvivorDied removes from queries, keeps record for history
xUnit: same seed → same 4 survivors; no Tough+Frail; effective skill clamps
ui: Roster list: name, health/mood bars, top 2 skills (placeholder text, no portraits)
Survivor detail panel: skill bars and trait chips with tooltip descriptions

connections.why: needs gauges live on the survivor; Glutton changes hunger rate
connections.how: Needs is a component class owned by Survivor; NeedsSystem reads TraitFx.Mul(s, "appetite")
connections.godot: SimHost emits SurvivorChanged(id) signal; roster UI re-reads the record
connections.unity: SimHost raises C# event SurvivorChanged(int id); roster view subscribes in OnEnable

connections.why: skills decide who is good at which job and how fast
connections.how: Work output = hours × Skills.SkillMult(level) × condition factors, read via survivor id
connections.godot: Work tab OptionButton per survivor sends AssignJob command through SimHost
connections.unity: DropdownField per row sends AssignJob command via SimHost

connections.why: a battle unit is built from a survivor (aim from Shooting, HP from Health)
connections.how: BattleUnit.FromSurvivor(s) copies stats in; combat.resolve writes Health back by id
connections.godot: Battle scene spawns unit nodes keyed by survivor id
connections.unity: Battle prefab per unit holds survivor id, no sim data duplicated

connections.why: survivors are the core of every save
connections.how: Survivor is a plain class serialised by System.Text.Json; traits/skills stored as ids
connections.godot: No engine code: save is sim-only
connections.unity: No engine code: save is sim-only

godot.approach: No game logic in Godot: the Survivor lives in BrokenState.Sim. Godot only shows it: a roster scene (VBoxContainer of rows) that SimHost refreshes on a SurvivorChanged signal. Trait/skill icons come from the ArtCatalog by art key.

unity.approach: Same split: the Sim assembly owns Survivor; a RosterView (UI Toolkit) binds rows to survivor ids and redraws when SimHost raises SurvivorChanged. Do not make Survivor a MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject: it is runtime state that must save and test headless.

newb: Definitions vs instances: a TraitDef ("Tough") is static content in JSON; a survivor just holds the string "tough". This is the Type Object pattern and it keeps saves small and content editable.
Route every trait effect through one lookup (TraitFx). The prototype does this (traits.js traitFx) so a new trait is a JSON row, not 20 scattered if-statements.
Fewer stats is better: skills + traits already cover what attributes would. Each stat you add must be shown, balanced and explained.
Give the generator its own RNG stream so adding a survivor roll later does not change the map the same seed produces.
pitfalls: Storing references to other objects (a Base object) on Survivor: store ids, or saves and tests get tangled.
Letting UI code edit Health/Mood directly instead of sending commands.
Hard-coding trait checks (if traits.Contains("tough")) across systems instead of TraitFx.
test: xUnit: seeded generation is stable (snapshot of 4 survivors for seed 1234), clamps hold, opposite traits never co-occur, TraitFx returns 1.0 with no traits. Manual: start a run, see 4 distinct survivors with sensible skills; same seed shows the same crew.

title: Needs: hunger, thirst, sleep, mood
summary: Hourly gauges that make survivors people: hunger and thirst fall and are refilled from the stockpile, tiredness builds while awake and is slept off, and mood sums short-lived reasons ("Ate a meal", "Hungry").
whyHere: Needs turn the daily economy into pressure: without them food and water are just numbers. It sits right after the Survivor model and the clock, and before base.core, by reading food through a small interface.
subsystems: Eating & drinking from a food source
sliceScope: 3 needs + mood. Hunger falls 40/day, thirst 60/day (1.5× hunger, as the prototype); below 70 a survivor eats/drinks up to 100 from the base stock (1 food or 1 water unit fills 40/60). Tiredness +1/h awake, −3/h asleep, default sleep 22–06; Tired at 24 (aim −5), Exhausted at 36 (aim −12). Mood = 60 base + modifiers (Hungry −10, Thirsty −15, Tired −5, Ate −0 …) each with an end hour. On a team they eat from the party's supplies. Below 15 hunger/thirst: health loss.
fullScope: Person-by-person meal breaks at 06/12/20 with a fullness target 80–100, a meal mood ladder, food preferences (Vegetarian, Picky), base ration levels (lean ×0.8, feast ×1.5), short rations under 7 days of food (60%), the cold (+10–20% food below 0°C), season thirst (summer ×1.3, hot day ×1.6), watch shifts and sleeping in. Mental breaks and comforts are surv.morale; food types and cooking are econ.food.

data: content/needs.json: rates per day, eat thresholds (eat below 70 to 100), starving line (15), tired/exhausted lines (24/36), sleep window
content/moods.json: thought defs {id, label, amount, hours} (Hungry, Thirsty, Tired, Exhausted, AteMeal, SleptWell)
Needs component on Survivor (Hunger, Thirst, Tired, Moods list) + save mapping
backend: NeedsSystem.TickHour(world): decay, sleep/awake, apply thresholds → add/remove thoughts
IFoodSource interface (TryTake(SupplyId, n)) implemented by Base stockpile and Party supplies; eating pulls from the survivor's current location
Mood = clamp(base + Σ active thoughts); expire thoughts by hour
NeedFactor(s) for work speed and aim (used by base.work and combat)
Emit events: SurvivorStarving, SurvivorExhausted (for the log/cards)
xUnit: 24h with food keeps gauges level; no food → hunger hits 0 by ~2.5 days; thirst runs out first
ui: Three small bars + mood number on each roster row; tooltip lists active thoughts with their +/−
Status chips (Hungry, Tired) for the hub screen

connections.why: at home they eat and drink from the stockpile
connections.how: Base implements IFoodSource; NeedsSystem calls source.Take("food", 1)
connections.godot: Stock panel listens to the StockChanged signal to update counts
connections.unity: Stock view subscribes to SimHost.StockChanged

connections.why: the daily ledger and forecasts must agree with what needs actually ate
connections.how: NeedsSystem records consumption into the base's DailyLedger; forecast uses the same per-day rates from NeedsDef
connections.godot: End-of-day report popup reads the ledger after DayEnded signal
connections.unity: DayEnded C# event opens the report panel

connections.why: sleep hours and exhaustion decide who works this hour
connections.how: Scheduler asks Sleep.IsSleepHour(s, hour) and NeedFactor(s)
connections.godot: Activity label per survivor updates on hourly tick signal
connections.unity: Activity label refresh on SimHost.HourTicked

connections.why: away from base, needs drain from the team's packed supplies
connections.how: Party implements IFoodSource; same NeedsSystem, different source by Location
connections.godot: Team panel shows days of food left
connections.unity: Team panel shows days of food left

godot.approach: Needs run in the sim's hourly tick, not in _Process. The hub UI shows three ProgressBars per survivor and re-reads them when SimHost emits HourTicked. Thought tooltips use Control.TooltipText or a small custom tooltip panel.

unity.approach: Same: the sim ticks needs; a UI Toolkit row template has three ProgressBars bound to the survivor id and refreshed on SimHost.HourTicked. Keep UI pull-based (read on event) rather than pushing every value change.

newb: A need is just a number that drifts and a threshold that triggers something. Keep rates in JSON so you can tune by playtest without recompiling.
Mood as a list of timed 'thoughts' (RimWorld's approach) is easy to explain to the player: the tooltip IS the formula.
Tick needs per game-hour, not per frame: at 5× speed frames and hours drift apart, and per-frame logic would break determinism and saves.
Use an interface (IFoodSource) so needs do not care whether food comes from a base or a backpack: same rule everywhere, also for AI groups (ADR 0001).
pitfalls: Eating in one system and counting upkeep in another with different numbers: forecasts then lie. One source of truth.
Forgetting that time skipping (travel, sleep) must run every hour, not just the last one.
Mood that only goes down: add positive thoughts (ate, rested) or players feel punished.
test: xUnit: 72 simulated hours with full stock keeps hunger/thirst above 60 and consumes ~3 food, ~3 water per person; empty stock → Starving event and health loss; awake 24h → Tired thought. Manual: run 3 days at 5×, watch bars dip and refill; empty the water cheat → thirst crashes first.

title: Wounds, healing, death (basic)
summary: Health 0–100 per survivor: damage from battles and starving lowers it, wounds can turn infected, rest and a medic with meds heal it, and at 0 the survivor dies and the game reacts.
whyHere: The slice's loop ends with 'wounded heal, someone may die': battle damage needs a home before combat.resolve exists. It depends only on the Survivor model and the clock.
sliceScope: One Health number plus a Wound flag set: Severe (<30), Infected. Hurt(amount, cause) applies trait multipliers (Tough ×0.75, Frail ×1.25); a hit of 10+ has a 25% chance to need dressing, undressed for a day → may turn infected. Healing at base 4/day + 0.4 × best Medicine; infected halves healing and drains 3/day; no healing while the base is out of food or water. One treatment a day by the Medic job: 1 meds, clears infection, +10. Severe survivors rest (no work). Health 0 → death: event, log line, items to base stock, removed from roster.
fullScope: Hospital tiers (infirmary → field hospital → clinic → trauma hospital) with medic staffing and bed caps, surgery on severe wounds, admit lines, auto-treat with a meds reserve; illnesses (camp fever, wound fever, flu season, contagion by headcount), the worm, medic training, battlefield medics and a downed state. Grief and the memorial wall on death.

data: content/health.json: severe line (30), base heal/day (4), medicine factor (0.4), infection drain (3/day), dressing chance (0.25), treatment meds cost
Wound fields on Survivor (Severe derived, Infected, NeedsDressingSinceHour) + save mapping
Death cause strings / log templates ("died of an infected wound")
backend: Health.Hurt(world, s, amount, cause): trait multipliers, wound roll (own RNG stream), death at ≤0
Health.TickHour: healing rate formula, infection drain, healing blocked by base hunger/thirst days
Medical.DailyTreatment(base): worst first, one per patient a day, uses meds from stock, Medicine skill bonus
Death pipeline: Survivor.Alive=false, drop gear to location (base stock / party cargo / battle body), publish SurvivorDied
xUnit: 50 damage on Tough = 37.5; infected wound without meds kills in N days; healing paused with no food
ui: Health bar colour bands + Severe/Infected chips on roster
Death popup / log entry with cause; greyed survivor in history list

connections.why: battle damage and deaths come back to the campaign
connections.how: combat.resolve calls Health.Hurt with the unit's lost HP; units killed in battle go through the same death pipeline
connections.godot: Battle results screen lists wounded/dead from SurvivorDied events
connections.unity: Results panel built from the drained event queue

connections.why: badly hurt people rest; the Medic job does the treating
connections.how: Scheduler checks Health.IsSevere → Rest; Medic job slots feed Medical.DailyTreatment
connections.godot: Activity label shows "Resting (wounded)"
connections.unity: Activity label shows "Resting (wounded)"

connections.why: a death or infection can raise a decision card
connections.how: Card system subscribes to SurvivorDied / WoundInfected events
connections.godot: Card popup scene opened by SimHost on CardRaised signal
connections.unity: Card UIDocument shown on CardRaised event

connections.why: an infirmary speeds healing
connections.how: Healing reads base.Buildings.Has("infirmary") bonus from building effects
connections.godot: Building tooltip shows the heal bonus
connections.unity: Building tooltip shows the heal bonus

godot.approach: Health is pure sim. Godot shows a coloured ProgressBar (theme override per band) and listens for SurvivorDied to play a placeholder sting and open a popup. Keep death presentation separate from the death rule.

unity.approach: Sim owns health; a UI Toolkit ProgressBar with USS classes per band (ok / hurt / severe). SimHost converts SurvivorDied to a C# event; a DeathPopup controller shows it.

newb: Start with a single health number; RimWorld-style per-body-part wounds are a big jump in UI and balance. The prototype itself uses one number plus flags.
Death is an event, not a deletion: keep the record (Alive=false) so history, grief and 'Why?' explanations can find them later.
Make every number (heal rate, infection drain) data-driven so Hardcore mode can scale them later with a multiplier.
pitfalls: Deleting a dead survivor while other systems still hold their id (party member lists, jobs).
Applying damage in the UI or battle view code instead of through Health.Hurt: trait multipliers get skipped.
Healing that ignores hunger: the prototype blocks healing while the base has no food or water, which is what makes shortages scary.
test: xUnit: trait multipliers, death at exactly 0, infection progression, treatment uses one meds and clears infection, healing blocked on hunger days. Manual: cheat-wound a survivor to 25, watch them rest and heal over days; remove meds and let an infected one die → popup + log.

title: Items, stacks & inventory (slots, weight)
summary: Everything a survivor can hold: item definitions from JSON, item instances that can stack, and a personal inventory of equipment slots, pockets and a pack, limited by weight. Bulk supplies (food, water, wood, rounds) stay as counts, not items.
whyHere: Weapons, loot, the stockpile's armory and the battle's search/reload all move items. It needs content (ItemDef) and survivors; weapons and loot build directly on it.
sliceScope: ~20 item defs (3 guns, 2 melee, ammo boxes per calibre, bandage, meds kit, backpack, crowbar, flashlight, food can, water bottle…). Slots: Hands, Body, Back (pack), 4 Pockets; a pack has 6 slots. Stackables merge up to StackMax and split. Max load 40 kg (Strong Back later). A MoveItem command validates slot type, small-only pockets, stack rules and weight. Survivors on a team carry; the base holds an Armory list of loose items.
fullScope: RPG slots for weapon, off hand tool, sidearm, belt melee, sling, ear pro, body/head/arms/legs armour and pack; rig pouches by kind; loose vs boxed rounds and bulk ammo cans; supplies taken out of stores as carriable items; two-handed carried things; load bands that slow travel; item condition and salvage. Prototype item data spans GEAR, ~146 guns, dozens of blades and kits.

data: content/items.json: id, name, kg, value, slot kind, small (fits pocket), stackMax, tags[], artKey
content/supplies.json: bulk supply ids (food, water, wood, scrap, meds, ammo_9mm…) with kg per unit
ItemInstance + Inventory runtime classes with stable instance ids + save mapping
ContentDb validation tests: every item has an art key, positive weight, unique id
backend: Inventory API: CanPlace(item, slot), Place, Remove, Find; Weight(s); MaxLoad(s) via TraitFx
Stacks: Merge(a,b) up to StackMax, Split(item, n), UseOne(item)
MoveItem command: from/to ItemLocation (survivor slot, pack slot, base armory, party cargo, container) with clear refusal reasons
Location addressing as a typed record (not strings like the prototype's "s:12:pocket:3")
xUnit: weight sums, pocket refuses large items, merge overflow leaves remainder, moving across locations only at the same place
ui: Placeholder paper-doll: slot boxes + pocket row + pack grid with item names/icons from ArtCatalog; weight line "23.4 / 40 kg"
Drag-and-drop between slots (or click-to-select then click-to-place) sending MoveItem; red flash + reason on refusal

connections.why: a weapon is an item with extra combat data
connections.how: WeaponDef keyed by the same item id; Inventory.Hands gives the equipped weapon
connections.godot: Weapon panel reads the Hands slot item
connections.unity: Weapon panel reads the Hands slot item

connections.why: loot rolls produce ItemInstances and supply counts
connections.how: LootRoller returns List<ItemInstance> + Dictionary<supplyId,int>; MoveItem takes them out of a container
connections.godot: Search window shows container contents beside the doll
connections.unity: Search window shows container contents beside the doll

connections.how: UI only sends MoveItem/Split commands and re-reads Inventory on InventoryChanged(ownerId)
connections.godot: Control._GetDragData/_CanDropData/_DropData on slot Controls
connections.unity: UI Toolkit pointer events / manipulators on slot VisualElements

connections.why: loose items at home live in the base armory and count toward storage kg
connections.how: Base.Armory is an item list; Storage.UsedKg adds item weights
connections.godot: Armory tab lists items
connections.unity: Armory tab lists items

connections.why: weight carried slows and limits a team
connections.how: Party load = Σ member Inventory.Weight + share of cargo; checked against MaxLoad
connections.godot: Team panel shows load bar
connections.unity: Team panel shows load bar

godot.approach: Build each slot as a Control (Panel + TextureRect icon + count Label). Godot's built-in drag-and-drop virtuals on Control (_GetDragData, _CanDropData, _DropData) map neatly onto MoveItem: _CanDropData asks the sim's CanPlace, _DropData sends the command. Icons come from the ArtCatalog Resource by art key.

unity.approach: UI Toolkit: a UXML template per slot, a grid for the pack; implement drag with PointerDown/Move/Up events (or a PointerManipulator) and call the sim's CanPlace/MoveItem. Item icons via an ArtCatalog ScriptableObject mapping art keys to Sprites.

newb: ItemDef (shared, read-only) vs ItemInstance (this particular box with 37 rounds): the Flyweight idea. Never copy the def's fields onto every instance.
Keep bulk goods (food, wood, rounds in base stock) as counts in a dictionary. Making 900 wood into 900 objects kills performance and saves, which is why the prototype pools supplies.
All inventory changes go through one validated MoveItem command: UI, AI groups and tests use the same door, so rules cannot be bypassed.
Weight is the real limit; slots only say where something is. That keeps the rules simple to explain.
pitfalls: Duplicating items on a failed move (remove succeeded, add failed): do moves as check-then-apply.
Instance ids that are not saved: references from equipment/jobs break after load.
Building drag-and-drop logic into the UI that the AI and tests can't use.
test: xUnit: place/move/split/merge suite, weight limit refusals, round-trip save of a full inventory. Manual: drag a pistol from the armory to Hands, ammo box into a pocket, try to put a backpack in a pocket (refused with reason), split a stack of 6 cans 3/3.

title: Weapons & ammo (basic: a few guns & melee)
summary: The combat numbers behind weapon items: damage range, optimal range and falloff, aim bonus, noise, magazine size and calibre for guns; damage and skill scaling for melee. Ammo is counted by calibre.
whyHere: Battles (combat.actions, combat.los, combat.ai) need weapon numbers and an ammo rule, and loot needs weapons to find. It builds on items and survivor skills.
sliceScope: 3 guns and 2 melee, using the prototype's numbers: 9mm pistol (dmg 15–22, opt range 6, aim +4, cap 15, noise 2), pump shotgun (24–36, opt 4, aim +10 close, cap 6, noise 3), hunting rifle .308 (31–43, opt 8, cap 5, noise 3); kitchen knife (14–22, silent) and baseball bat (15–24). 3 calibres as supplies (9mm, 12ga, .308). A gun stores LoadedRounds; Reload fills from ammo stacks the shooter carries. Shooting/Melee skill adds aim/damage; below a weapon's required skill, a penalty.
fullScope: Physical round stacks in firing order inside guns and magazines; ammo types (FMJ, HP, AP, subsonic, rubber) per calibre with damage/pen; spare magazines and reload sources costing 1–2 actions; fire modes, jams by reliability, suppression (gear.ballistics); attachments and the gun builder (gear.gunbuilder); ~146 guns, blades with quick strikes/bleed/stagger, launchers, non-lethal weapons, throwables.

data: content/weapons.json keyed by item id: kind (gun|melee), dmgMin/Max, optRange, falloff, aim, apCost, noise, cap, calibre, reqSkill
content/calibres.json: id, name, kg per round, box size (9mm 50), art key
Gun state on ItemInstance (LoadedRounds) + save mapping
backend: Weapons.Of(item) lookup; DamageRoll(rng, weapon, skill) with crit chance
RangeModifier(weapon, distance): full to optRange, then −falloff per tile
Reload(unit/survivor, gun): take rounds of the gun's calibre from own pockets/pack (not teammates), fill to cap, report rounds used
Skill gap rule: aim penalty per level below reqSkill
xUnit: damage within range, reload stops at cap and at available rounds, wrong calibre never loads
ui: Weapon tooltip: damage, range, rounds "12/15", noise as a 0–3 meter
Rounds badge on the gun's inventory icon

connections.why: Shoot/Melee/Reload actions use these numbers
connections.how: Actions call Weapons.DamageRoll and Weapons.Reload; spend Loaded per shot
connections.godot: Action bar buttons enabled by sim CanShoot/CanReload queries
connections.unity: Action bar buttons enabled by sim CanShoot/CanReload queries

connections.why: hit chance combines range, aim and cover
connections.how: HitChance = base + weapon.Aim + skill − RangeModifier − cover
connections.godot: Hit % label over the target
connections.unity: Hit % label over the target

connections.why: gunshots make noise the dead hear
connections.how: Shot publishes NoiseEvent(position, weapon.Noise); dead AI reads it
connections.godot: Placeholder noise ring effect at the shooter
connections.unity: Placeholder noise ring effect at the shooter

connections.why: guns and ammo are what players hunt for
connections.how: Loot tables reference weapon item ids and calibre supply ids
connections.godot: n/a (sim only)
connections.unity: n/a (sim only)

godot.approach: Pure data + sim. Godot only displays weapon stats (tooltip panel) and a rounds badge; later a Resource subclass can attach placeholder sprites/sounds per weapon art key without touching the sim's WeaponDef.

unity.approach: Weapon numbers stay in JSON loaded by the sim (not in ScriptableObjects) so tests and both engines share them. A WeaponArt ScriptableObject maps art keys to sprites/audio clips for presentation only.

newb: A damage range (15–22) with a flat roll is easy to read; Red Blob's damage-rolls article shows how to make it feel less swingy if needed.
Ammo by calibre is what makes loot exciting: a .308 rifle with no .308 is a decision. Keep that rule even in the slice.
Noise is a weapon stat, not a sound file: the AI reacts to the number; audio is added later on top.
Store loaded rounds on the gun instance so a reload in one battle carries into the next (the prototype's 'guns leave loaded').
pitfalls: Hard-coding weapon numbers in combat code; balancing then needs recompiles.
A reload that pulls from the base stockpile mid-battle: only what the shooter carries.
Building magazines/ammo types into the slice: that is gear.ballistics later.
test: xUnit: per-weapon damage bounds over 10k seeded rolls, falloff values, reload edge cases (empty, partial, wrong calibre), skill gap penalty. Manual: equip the shotgun, fire 6 times in a test battle, reload from a pocket box; rounds badge matches.

title: Base entity & stockpile (supplies, storage)
summary: A Base is a place on the State Map where survivors live: its residents, a stockpile of bulk supplies (food, water, wood, meds, scrap, rounds), an armory of loose items, beds and a storage capacity in kg.
whyHere: Needs eat from it, buildings are built at it, work produces into it and loot lands in it. It must exist before buildings, work and the daily economy.
sliceScope: One hub base on the start hex with 4 residents. Stock dictionary for ~8 supplies (food, water, wood, scrap, meds, ammo_9mm, ammo_12ga, ammo_308). Armory list of items. Storage = 1200 kg core + storage buildings; overflow is only shown as "outside" (no wear yet). Beds = from buildings. TransferSupplies command between base and a party on the same hex. Ledger records each day's produced/used per supply.
fullScope: Base tiers camp (0 kg) / shelter (150) / outpost (500) / hub (1200), storage ladder from storage box 60 kg to warehouse 6000 kg, containers and bins, goods outside wearing 2%/day (×2 wet) and raided first, food lots with spoilage, water capacity separate, woodpile not counted; several bases, supply runs and hauling, a 500×500 base map with placed buildings, hidden bases, sieges.

data: Base runtime class: Id, Name, Hex, Tier, Stock, Armory, Ledger + save mapping
content/supplies.json fields used here: kg per unit, stored (bool: wood/water not counted)
content/base_tiers.json: core storage kg per tier (slice uses hub only)
backend: Stockpile API: Has, Take (returns what was taken), Add; implements IFoodSource for surv.needs
Storage.UsedKg/CapacityKg/OutsideKg (stock by kg + armory item weights; buildings add capacity)
Residents query by survivor Location; Beds from building effects
TransferSupplies / TransferItem commands base⇄party with validation (same hex, enough stock, party carry room)
DailyLedger: Record(supply, delta, reason); rolled over at day end
xUnit: take never goes negative, overflow math, transfer conserves totals
ui: Hub 'Stock' tab: supply table with counts and today's +/−, storage bar "860 / 1200 kg"
Armory list (reuses ui.inventory item rows)

connections.why: residents eat and drink from the stock
connections.how: Base implements IFoodSource; Take() records into the ledger with reason "eaten"
connections.godot: StockChanged signal refreshes the stock tab
connections.unity: StockChanged C# event refreshes the stock view

connections.why: teams pack supplies out and bring loot home
connections.how: TransferSupplies command; arrival at the base hex auto-unloads cargo
connections.godot: Team-forming screen shows base stock beside party packs
connections.unity: Team-forming panel shows base stock beside party packs

connections.why: loot from a raid lands in the stockpile
connections.how: On PartyArrived at home: cargo items → Armory, supplies → Stock, ledger reason "loot"
connections.godot: Arrival toast lists what came in
connections.unity: Arrival toast lists what came in

connections.why: the hub screens are mostly views of this
connections.how: Read-only queries + commands; refresh on StockChanged/DayEnded
connections.godot: TabContainer with Stock/Roster/Build/Work tabs
connections.unity: UIDocument with tab buttons switching panels

godot.approach: The base is sim data; in Godot the hub is a scene with a TabContainer. The Stock tab is a Tree (columns: supply, count, today) rebuilt on StockChanged. The base's marker on the State Map is drawn by ui.statemap from Base.Hex.

unity.approach: A HubScreen UIDocument with tab panels; the stock table is a MultiColumnListView bound to a list of (supply, count, delta) rows built from the sim on StockChanged. No MonoBehaviour per base: the base is not a GameObject.

newb: Bases are data, not scenes or GameObjects. The view is built from the data; this makes saving and AI groups (which run the same base rules, ADR 0001) trivial.
A ledger with reasons ("eaten", "built bunkhouse", "loot") costs little and pays back hugely: the end-of-day report and 'why am I out of food?' come for free.
Storage as kg rather than slot counts is easy to reason about and matches the prototype's one rule: nothing is refused, overflow just lies outside.
pitfalls: Stock going negative because two systems took the last unit in the same tick: Take returns what it actually took.
Storing supply names as display strings: use ids and look up names.
Building multi-base logic now: one hub is enough; keep the code base-id driven so more bases drop in later (econ.hauling).
test: xUnit: stock arithmetic, storage capacity/overflow, transfer conservation (total food in world unchanged by a transfer), ledger sums equal stock change. Manual: the Stock tab shows starting supplies; pack food into a team and see stock drop; send them home and see it return.

title: Buildings & construction queue (slice: 4–5 buildings)
summary: Building definitions in JSON (cost, build hours, limits, effects such as beds, storage, water or food) and a per-base construction queue that builders work through hour by hour.
whyHere: The slice asks the player to queue 1–2 buildings; buildings also give beds, storage and production that the economy reads. It needs the base and its stockpile first.
subsystems: Effects (beds, storage kg, water, food, healing)
sliceScope: 5 buildings, abstract (no placement grid; the hub has a few plots): Farm plot (40 wood, 4 h, food with a farmer), Rain catcher (water/day, more in rain), Bunkhouse (+6 beds), Storage crates (+150 kg), Infirmary (+healing, needs Medicine 2 to staff). QueueBuild checks cost, max count and a skill req, deducts materials at start; each builder-hour adds hours × skill mult; done → BuildingCompleted. Cancel refunds all, demolish refunds half.
fullScope: ~85 building defs: plots by base size, general buildings with fittings (bunk beds, shelves 150 kg, lockers 100 kg), upgrade chains (crafting bench → workbench → master workbench needing Mechanics 2/5), stations (ammo bench, med station, machine shop), storage ladder to warehouse 6000 kg, tool and blueprint requirements, building materials and sheets, power, breakdowns and repairs, placement on the 500×500 base map, field works outside the walls.

title: Work assignment & job scheduler (slice: simple roles)
summary: Each survivor at a base has one job (Build, Farm, Fetch water, Scavenge, Medic, Guard, Rest); every game-hour a scheduler decides what they actually do (sleep, rest if hurt, else their job) and job systems turn those hours into output.
whyHere: Buildings, farming, water and healing all need 'who is working on what this hour'. It joins survivors, needs and health to the base's systems, so it comes after those cards.
sliceScope: One job per survivor from 7 roles in JSON. Hourly: sleep hours → asleep; Severe wound → rest; else on the job. Work factor = skill mult × health/tired/mood factors (e.g. Exhausted ×0.7). Job systems pull workers: ConstructionSystem (Build), farm (Farm), water (Fetch water), scavenging, Medical (Medic), Guard (alertness for later). Each survivor gets an activity line ("Building bunkhouse", "Resting (wounded)", "Idle: nothing to build"). An 'Assign idle' button picks the base's most urgent job.
fullScope: RimWorld-style priorities: 19 work types with a 1–5 grid per role, role skill minimums, a 24-hour schedule per role (work/guard/free/sleep letters), emergencies (raiders → Guard, horde → hold limit), watch roster with shifts, no-idle helpers who keep their role, leaders and stewards, an idle planner by base need, the governor; job trips outside the walls.

data: content/jobs.json: id, name, verb ("Building"), skill used, needs (e.g. Build needs a queued job), artKey
Survivor.JobId + runtime Activity (jobId, reason) + save

WorkScheduler.TickHour(base): ordered rules (asleep → rest if hurt → job), producing Activity per survivor
WorkFactor(s): skill mult × NeedFactor × health factor (one function used by every job)
Job registry: IJobSystem { string JobId; bool HasWork(base); void Work(base, workers, hours) }
IdlePlanner.Suggest(base): rank needs (water short, food short, build queued) → job per idle survivor

godot.approach: The scheduler is a sim function run on each game hour. The Work tab is a GridContainer (name | job OptionButton | skill | activity). OptionButton.ItemSelected sends AssignJob via SimHost; rows refresh on HourTicked.

unity.approach: A MultiColumnListView (name, job DropdownField, skill, activity). The dropdown's value-changed callback sends AssignJob; rows rebind on SimHost.HourTicked.

newb: The scheduler is a tiny state machine: each hour a survivor is in one state (Asleep, Resting, Working, Idle) chosen by an ordered list of rules. Write the rules top-down; the first that matches wins.
Always store WHY with WHAT (Activity.Reason). Players forgive a lot when the game explains itself; the prototype shows a reason on every idle worker.
One WorkFactor function used by every job keeps tiredness, wounds and skill effects consistent.
Start with one job per person; the RimWorld priority grid (base.workgrid) can replace the job choice later without changing the IJobSystem side.
pitfalls: Each job system checking sleep/health on its own: put those rules once in the scheduler.
Running job output per frame instead of per game-hour.
Silent idle workers: always surface idle with a reason.

title: Daily economy & upkeep (consumption, production)
summary: The day-end pass for every base: production (farm food, rain and well water, wood, scavenged scrap), upkeep (heating wood in the cold), short rations when food runs low, and a report and forecast of days of food and water left.
whyHere: This is where the slice's 'food, water, wood' loop closes, and it gives the player the numbers to plan expeditions. It needs the base, buildings, work and needs in place.
sliceScope: 3 tracked goods: food, water, wood (+scrap from scavenging). At midnight per base: farm plots × farmers × skill → food (seasonless for the slice); rain catchers → water (×2 on a rain day from core.weather); fetch-water and wood jobs add their hours' output; heating burns wood per head below 0°C. Eating stays in surv.needs (hourly) and is only reported here. Under 7 days of food → short rations (60%) with a mood thought. Forecast = stock ÷ per-day use. Shortage warnings at 3 days → event/card.
fullScope: Water production by wells/streams/rain with capacity, purification and the worm, summer evaporation and a summer water warning; farming by crop and season, winter's lean months; hunting, fishing, foraging and job trips; stations and crafting output; food lots spoiling by storage; supply lines and trade routes between bases; illness, recruits and hub events on the daily list; ledger charts.

data: content/economy.json: yields per worker-hour by job, per-building daily output, heating wood per head and temperature line, ration share (0.6) and trigger (7 days)
DailyReport record (per base, per supply: produced / used / by reason) kept for the last N days in the save
backend: EconomySystem.DayEnd(world): fixed, documented step order (produce → heat → ration check → report → warnings)
Production: one function per source reading building effects, workers and weather
Forecast(base, supply): uses the SAME rates as needs/upkeep (call the shared functions, never copy numbers)
Rationing toggle + thought; ShortageWarning event at ≤3 days
xUnit: a balanced 4-person base stays stable 7 days; no farmer → food forecast drops by 4/day; cold day burns wood
ui: End-of-day report popup (skippable): per supply in/out with reasons
Days-left chips on the hub header (Food 9d, Water 3d ⚠, Wood 20d)

newb: Write the day-end as an explicit ordered list of steps. Order matters (produce before eat? heat before ration check?) and an explicit list makes it visible and testable.
Forecasts must call the same functions as the real consumption; the prototype's comments stress this ('so the stores and every forecast agree').
Balance with a headless test: simulate 30 days of a 4-person base with no input and print the stock curve. That is your first balance tool (meta.balance grows from it).
pitfalls: Double-counting food: hourly eating in needs AND a daily upkeep subtraction here.
Random production with the global RNG: use the economy's own stream so a new feature doesn't shift harvests.
Too many goods in the slice: 3 is plenty to learn from.
test: xUnit: a 7-day golden run for seed X matches a stored stock table; ration trigger at <7 days; heating only below the line. Manual: play 7 days at 5×, read the daily reports; remove the farmer and watch the food forecast fall and the warning card appear.

title: Loot tables & containers
summary: What can be found where: weighted loot tables in JSON, container kinds (kitchen cabinet, locker, desk, car trunk) that point to tables, and a seeded roller that fills a container once, the first time it is opened.
whyHere: POIs, raid maps and search actions all need loot; it sits just before battles so the slice's 'search containers, extract with loot' works. It needs items, weapons and the RNG.
sliceScope: 4 tables (house kitchen, house bedroom, garage, police car) and 5 container kinds, used by the slice's one building template. Entries: item or supply id, weight or chance, min–max count, or a nested table. Roll on first search with an RNG stream seeded from (world seed, POI id, container id), store the result; re-opening never re-rolls. Contents move to survivors via MoveItem. An audit test checks every slice item is findable and every table entry exists.
fullScope: Site-type loot pools and per-container tables (gun racks, evidence lockers, ammo crates, fire engines…) with theme tags checked over 100 buildings a kind (±10%), small 'finds' rolled separately, gun distribution tables by site, blades/tools/helmets on their own dice, item condition by source, lock boxes opened with the right tool, 18% of plain dead carrying a former survivor's kit, Hardcore's scarce loot, hour-by-hour abstract scavenging with Heat, shared finite loot AI groups also take.

data: content/loot_tables.json: id, rolls (min–max), entries [{item|supply|table, weight, min, max}]
content/containers.json: kind, name, table id, search AP cost, artKey

Container.OpenOrSearch(): roll once, then expose contents as an ItemLocation for MoveItem

xUnit: 10k rolls match weights within tolerance; same seed same contents; second open does not re-roll
ui: Search window: container contents list beside the survivor's inventory; Take / Take all
Dev overlay: show a container's table id and rolled contents (debug only)

godot.approach: Sim-only rolling. In the battle scene each container is a node (Area2D or clickable Sprite) holding its container id; clicking sends a Search command through SimHost and the search window opens on the ContainerOpened signal. Loot tables are not Godot Resources: they stay JSON for the sim.

unity.approach: Each container in the battle view is a GameObject with a small ContainerView MonoBehaviour storing the id; clicks send Search via SimHost; the search window is a UI Toolkit panel listing contents. Do not use ScriptableObjects for loot tables, keep them in JSON shared with tests.

newb: Weighted random: sum the weights, roll 0..sum, walk the list until you pass the roll. Nested tables (an entry that points to another table) give you 'a random gun' without copying gun lists everywhere.
Roll once and store: if contents were re-rolled on every open, save-scumming and reloading would change loot. Seeding by (world, POI, container) makes it reproducible even before it is rolled.
Theme tags plus an automated audit is how the prototype keeps 'no military radios in a pharmacy' true across hundreds of tables. Start the audit test in the slice while tables are small.
pitfalls: Using the world's main RNG for loot: every new roll elsewhere changes all loot (determinism tests break).
Item ids typed by hand in tables with no validation: one typo is an empty drop. Validate on load.
Generous slice loot: tune scarcity early or the economy has no pressure.
test: xUnit: distribution within ±2% over 10k rolls, nested table resolution, deterministic per-container seed, roll-once, audit passes. Manual: raid the slice building twice from the same save: identical contents; search a container, take a pistol and 9mm box into pockets, extract, see it in the base armory.
